ru.title: Мостование концепций: оценка креативности мультимодальных моделей через китайские идиомы
ru.desc: В этой работе авторы предлагают C4 — оценочный фреймворк для измерения творческих способностей мультимодальных языковых моделей на основе китайских идиом (чэнъюй). Фреймворк использует кодирование концепций через мостовые пути в аннотированной сети кроссконцептуальных связей, позволяя генерировать задачи с явной структурой и контролируемой сложностью. Авторы создали набор данных C4-Eval с 884 тестовыми примерами и оценили 10 мультимодальных LLM, обнаружив значительный разрыв в способности моделей декодировать творчески закодированные смыслы через кроссконцептуальные отношения. Результаты показывают, что лучшие закрытые модели достигают только 50.7% точности, что подчеркивает вызов в оценке истинной креативности AI-систем.

en.title: Evaluating Creativity in MLLMs through Cross-Concept Understanding
en.desc: This paper discusses the evaluation of creative capabilities in machine learning language models (MLLMs), particularly in tasks that require understanding complex conceptual relationships. It introduces a new framework called C4, which focuses on cross-concept encoding and decoding to assess creativity through the use of Chinese idioms (Chengyu). The framework allows for the generation of structured items that test the models' ability to recover intended meanings from non-obvious connections. Results show that while some models perform better than others, there is a significant gap in their ability to creatively decode meanings based on cross-concept relations.

zh.title: 评估多语言大模型的创造力能力
zh.desc: 本论文探讨了多语言大模型（MLLMs）在设计、沟通、教育和人机协作中的创造能力评估。我们提出了C4评估框架，专注于基于成语的跨概念创造力，利用跨概念编码和解码来评估模型的理解能力。通过构建C4评估集，我们收集了184个合成项目和37个人工创建的跨概念成语，手动审查其关系和推理过程。研究结果显示，当前的MLLMs在解码创造性编码意义方面存在显著差距。

papers.title: Adversarial Attacks for Good: A Survey of Proactive Protection across the Visual Content Lifecycle
papers.abstract: Abstract  Once visual content enters an AI pipeline, its owner often retains little technical control over how it is used. Legal and regulatory remedies can address misuse, but many technical interventions must be applied earlier, when content is released or accessed. This survey examines the protective paradigm that has grown around this intervention point, which we call adversarial attacks for good. Perturbations and structured signals long studied as attacks on learned models are instead applied by data owners, creators, platforms, or auditors to disrupt unauthorized automation or support later accountability. Five research communities have arrived at this inversion largely independently, each addressing a different stage of a visual asset's lifecycle: privacy filters against unwanted recognition at sharing time, unlearnable examples against unauthorized training, generative safeguards against malicious editing or imitation, adversarial CAPTCHAs for access control against automated agents, and provenance mechanisms for post-circulation attribution. Although developed in separate venues with incompatible success criteria, many of these methods exploit persistent gaps between human perception, semantic interpretation, and machine inference, suggesting that the paradigm remains relevant as visual pipelines evolve toward multimodal models and autonomous agents. To make their claims comparable, we evaluate all five families along shared axes of transferability, adaptability, and deployment readiness. Across the lifecycle, we find that most protections are still validated mainly against static or weakly adaptive adversaries, while evidence beyond controlled benchmarks remains scarce. We close by consolidating cross-stage countermeasures and open problems for robust, composable, and deployable owner-side protection.

ru.title: Защита авторских прав на изображения: adversarial техники на службе владельцев контента
ru.desc: Статья исследует парадигму защиты визуального контента от несанкционированного использования в AI-системах, называя её «adversarial attacks for good». Авторы анализируют пять подходов на разных этапах жизненного цикла визуальных данных: фильтры приватности, необучаемые примеры, защиты генеративных моделей, adversarial CAPTCHA и механизмы атрибуции. Все эти методы используют разрывы между восприятием человека и работой машинных моделей для защиты прав создателей контента. Исследование оценивает эффективность методов по критериям переносимости, адаптивности и готовности к развертыванию в реальных условиях.

en.title: Empowering Content Owners with Adversarial Defenses
en.desc: This paper discusses how visual content can be better protected when it is used in AI systems. It introduces the concept of 'adversarial attacks for good', where techniques typically used to attack models are instead employed by content owners to prevent misuse. The authors review five different approaches that address various stages of a visual asset's lifecycle, such as privacy filters and generative safeguards. They highlight the need for these methods to be more effective against evolving AI systems and suggest areas for future research to enhance protection mechanisms.

zh.title: 善用对抗攻击，保护视觉内容的未来
zh.desc: 这篇论文探讨了在人工智能处理视觉内容时，内容所有者如何保持对其使用的技术控制。作者提出了一种称为“善用对抗攻击”的保护范式，旨在通过数据所有者和平台在内容发布或访问时采取技术干预来防止滥用。研究涵盖了视觉资产生命周期的不同阶段，包括隐私过滤、不可学习示例、生成性保护、对抗性验证码和来源机制等。尽管这些方法在不同领域独立发展，但它们都利用了人类感知、语义理解和机器推理之间的差距，表明这一范式在视觉处理管道向多模态模型和自主代理演变时仍然具有重要意义。

papers.title: FATE: Frame-Level Audio-Visual Temporal Embedding
papers.abstract: Abstract  When a dog opens its mouth and barks, humans naturally recognize what the sound is and when it occurs. Building audio-visual models with this same ability requires representations that capture both semantic and temporal alignment. Current approaches fall short on one side or the other: embedding models match semantic but lose temporal information; synchronization models capture temporal offsets but lack semantic understanding. To bridge this gap, we propose FATE, Frame-level Audio-visual Temporal Embedding. Unlike prior embedding models that pool each modality into a single embedding and discard temporal information, FATE retains frame-level sequences, aligns them on the physical timeline, and computes similarity over strictly aligned frame pairs. Unlike synchronization models that output only an offset prediction, FATE encodes synchronization in a reusable embedding space, trained with a joint objective combining cross-video semantic and within-video temporal contrastive learning to capture both what sounds and when it occurs. Across three tasks, FATE surpasses the strongest baseline on temporal and semantic retrieval by a large margin, matches fully supervised methods on event localization in a zero-shot setting, and achieves the best correlation with human judgments as a generation evaluation metric. The source code can be found at https://github.com/guankaisi/FATE.
affiliations: Gaoling School of Artificial Intelligence, Renmin University of China

ru.title: Синхронизация смысла и времени в аудиовизуальных представлениях
ru.desc: Авторы предлагают FATE — метод для создания аудиовизуальных моделей, которые одновременно понимают семантическое содержание и временное выравнивание медиа. В отличие от предыдущих подходов, которые либо теряли временную информацию при объединении модальностей в один эмбеддинг, либо предсказывали только временные смещения без семантического понимания, FATE сохраняет последовательности на уровне кадров и выравнивает их на физической временной шкале. Модель обучается на комбинированной функции потерь, включающей контрастивное обучение между видео (для семантики) и внутри видео (для синхронизации), что позволяет захватывать как звучание, так и момент его возникновения. Метод показывает значительное улучшение по сравнению с базовыми моделями в задачах поиска и локализации событий, а также лучше всего коррелирует с оценками человека.

en.title: FATE: Bridging Sound and Timing in Audio-Visual Learning
en.desc: The paper introduces FATE, a novel model designed to improve audio-visual understanding by effectively capturing both semantic meaning and temporal alignment. Unlike traditional models that either focus on semantic embeddings or temporal synchronization, FATE retains detailed frame-level sequences and aligns them on a timeline for better analysis. It employs a joint training approach that combines cross-video semantic learning with within-video temporal contrastive learning, allowing it to understand both the content of sounds and their timing. The results demonstrate that FATE significantly outperforms existing methods in various tasks, achieving high accuracy in both temporal and semantic retrieval, as well as event localization.

zh.title: FATE：音视频时间对齐的新突破
zh.desc: 本文提出了一种新的音视频模型FATE，旨在同时捕捉语义和时间对齐信息。与传统模型不同，FATE保留了帧级序列，并在物理时间线上对其进行对齐，从而计算严格对齐的帧对之间的相似性。FATE通过结合跨视频语义学习和视频内时间对比学习的联合目标，能够有效地捕捉声音的内容及其发生的时间。实验结果表明，FATE在时间和语义检索任务中显著超越了现有的基线模型，并在事件定位任务中表现出色。

papers.title: Capek 0.5: An Execution-Centric Vision-Language Model for Embodied Intelligence
papers.abstract: Abstract  Vision-language models are increasingly serving as the reasoning core of embodied agents. Robot execution is inherently iterative: each action reshapes the scene and physical state, continually renewing what must be perceived, reasoned about, and verified. Meeting these demands requires complementary capabilities that differ in supervision signals, prediction formats, and verification criteria. Existing approaches typically develop these capabilities against isolated, task-specific objectives, leaving open how they should be organized and integrated around execution as a whole. We present Capek 0.5, an embodied vision-language model built around an execution-centric capability taxonomy. Rather than organizing training by datasets or tasks, the taxonomy groups embodied capabilities according to their functional roles throughout execution and comprises four capability families: Spatial Reasoning, Temporal Understanding, Action Guidance, and State Verification. Each capability is first acquired by a dedicated specialist through reinforcement learning with verifiable rewards from a shared backbone, and the specialists are then consolidated into a single inference-time model through weight-space merging followed by routed policy-space distillation. We instantiate Capek 0.5 at the 2B and 35B-A3B scales and evaluate it from three complementary perspectives: comprehensive benchmark suites including Capek-StateBench, a new benchmark for state verification; a controlled study of capability retention from specialists to the unified model; and closed-loop evaluation in simulated embodied environments. Capek 0.5 improves the large majority of matched benchmark rows over its initialization, retains all four specialized capabilities in one checkpoint with quantified losses, and transfers to closed-loop embodied task execution.

ru.title: Единая модель для всех этапов выполнения роботом: от восприятия до верификации
ru.desc: Авторы представляют Capek 0.5, модель зрения и языка для воплощённых агентов (роботов), которая организована вокруг четырёх ключевых способностей: пространственного рассуждения, понимания времени, руководства действиями и проверки состояния. Каждую способность отдельно обучают специализированные модели с использованием reinforcement learning, а затем объединяют в единую модель через объединение весов и дистилляцию в пространстве политик. Модель оценивается на комплексных бенчмарках, включая новый Capek-StateBench для проверки состояния, и демонстрирует эффективность как в синтетических окружениях, так и при переносе на реальные задачи робота. Подход позволяет сохранить все четыре специализированные способности в одной модели при минимальных потерях производительности.

en.title: Capek 0.5: Integrating Vision-Language Capabilities for Dynamic Task Execution
en.desc: This paper introduces Capek 0.5, a vision-language model designed for embodied agents that need to perform tasks in dynamic environments. It organizes capabilities based on their roles in the execution process rather than by specific tasks, creating a taxonomy that includes Spatial Reasoning, Temporal Understanding, Action Guidance, and State Verification. Each capability is developed through reinforcement learning, allowing specialists to learn effectively before being combined into a single model. The evaluation shows that Capek 0.5 outperforms previous models on benchmarks and successfully retains specialized skills for real-time task execution.

zh.title: 提升机器人推理能力的全新模型
zh.desc: 本论文介绍了一种名为Capek 0.5的视觉-语言模型，旨在提升机器人在执行任务时的推理能力。该模型通过将能力分为空间推理、时间理解、行动指导和状态验证四个类别，来组织和整合不同的执行能力。每种能力通过强化学习获得，并在共享的基础上进行合并，形成一个统一的推理模型。Capek 0.5在多个基准测试中表现出色，能够在闭环环境中有效执行任务。

papers.title: OneEmo: A Unified Multimodal Reasoning Model for Emotion Perception, Understanding, and Interaction
papers.abstract: Abstract  Multimodal Large Language Models (MLLMs) have demonstrated remarkable capabilities in emotional intelligence. However, prevailing research predominantly focuses on task-specific specialization, often neglecting inter-task synergy and leaving latent reasoning potential underexplored. To bridge this gap, we introduce OneEmo, a unified affective generalist capable of mastering emotion perception, comprehension, and interaction. For this purpose, we first construct EmoWorld-130K, a comprehensive dataset that distills specialized affective knowledge into explicit reasoning trajectories via a human-in-the-loop workflow. Supervised fine-tuning on this corpus reveals significant mutual benefits derived from multi-task learning. Second, to fully unlock the latent reasoning potential, we propose Emo-Chord, a novel reinforcement learning strategy that stabilizes optimization through unified multi-task reward allocation. Extensive experiments demonstrate that OneEmo achieves state-of-the-art performance against similarly sized baselines across most benchmarks. Notably, despite having significantly fewer parameters than commercial models, OneEmo delivers highly competitive results. This paper paves the way for more reliable and interpretable affective computing. The code is available at https://github.com/waHAHJIAHAO/OneEmo.

ru.title: Единый эмоциональный помощник с синергией многозадачного обучения
ru.desc: В работе представлена OneEmo — единая мультимодальная языковая модель, которая объединяет восприятие, понимание и взаимодействие с эмоциями в одной системе. Авторы создали специализированный датасет EmoWorld-130K с явными цепочками рассуждений об эмоциях, полученными через активное участие людей. Для полного раскрытия потенциала модели предложен новый метод обучения с подкреплением Emo-Chord, который стабилизирует оптимизацию через единую многозадачную систему награждения. Экспериментальные результаты показывают, что OneEmo достигает наилучших показателей среди сопоставимых по размеру моделей, при этом уступая коммерческим системам лишь по количеству параметров.

en.title: OneEmo: Unifying Emotion Understanding for Enhanced AI Interaction
en.desc: This paper presents OneEmo, a Multimodal Large Language Model (MLLM) designed to enhance emotional intelligence by integrating various tasks related to emotion perception and interaction. The authors introduce EmoWorld-130K, a dataset that helps the model learn affective knowledge through structured reasoning paths, utilizing a human-in-the-loop approach. They also propose Emo-Chord, a reinforcement learning method that optimizes performance by distributing rewards across multiple tasks, leading to improved learning outcomes. The results show that OneEmo outperforms other models with fewer parameters, indicating its efficiency and effectiveness in affective computing.

zh.title: 情感智能的新纪元：OneEmo的崛起
zh.desc: 多模态大型语言模型（MLLMs）在情感智能方面展现了卓越的能力。然而，目前的研究主要集中在特定任务的专业化，往往忽视了任务间的协同作用，导致潜在推理能力未被充分探索。为了解决这个问题，我们提出了OneEmo，一个统一的情感通用模型，能够掌握情感感知、理解和互动。通过构建EmoWorld-130K数据集并采用监督微调和强化学习策略，我们的实验表明OneEmo在多个基准测试中表现出色，尽管参数量远少于商业模型，依然能提供竞争力的结果。

papers.title: Towards Interpretable Foundation Models for Retinal Fundus Images
papers.abstract: Abstract  Foundation models are used to extract transferable representations from large amounts of unlabeled data, typically via self-supervised learning (SSL). However, many of these models rely on architectures that offer limited interpretability, a critical issue in high-stakes domains such as medical imaging. We propose DualIFM, a foundation model that is interpretable-by-design via a BagNet backbone whose small receptive fields generate class evidence maps that are faithful to the model's decision-making process. Additionally, DualIFM incorporates a 2D projection layer during pretraining that enables direct visualization of the representation space, providing a dataset-level view of the learned structure including meaningful clinical clusters as well as potential spurious correlations. We trained DualIFM on over 800,000 color fundus photographs from various sources to learn generalizable representations for different downstream tasks. Our model achieves performance comparable to RETFound, which has 16times more parameters, while providing interpretable predictions on out-of-distribution data. These results suggest that large-scale SSL pretraining paired with inherent interpretability can lead to robust representations for retinal imaging. Code and pretrained models are available at github.com/berenslab/interpretable_FM.
affiliations: Hertie Institute for AI in Brain Health, University of Tübingen, Germany
Tübingen AI Center, University of Tübingen, Germany

ru.title: Интерпретируемая фундаментальная модель для медицинской диагностики без потери качества
ru.desc: В статье предлагается DualIFM — интерпретируемая фундаментальная модель, разработанная для анализа медицинских изображений, в частности снимков сетчатки глаза. Модель использует архитектуру BagNet с малыми рецептивными полями, которые генерируют карты доказательств класса, точно отражающие процесс принятия решений моделью. Во время предварительного обучения применяется слой 2D-проекции, позволяющий визуализировать пространство представлений и выявлять как клинически значимые кластеры, так и потенциально ложные корреляции. Модель обучена на более чем 800 тысячах фотографий глазного дна с использованием самообучения и достигает производительности, сравнимой с более сложными моделями, при этом сохраняя интерпретируемость предсказаний на данных из других распределений.

en.title: Interpretable Foundation Models for Medical Imaging
en.desc: This paper introduces DualIFM, a foundation model designed for better interpretability in machine learning, particularly in medical imaging. It uses a BagNet architecture that creates class evidence maps, allowing users to understand how the model makes decisions. The model also features a 2D projection layer that visualizes the learned representation space, highlighting important clinical patterns and potential biases. Trained on a large dataset of color fundus photographs, DualIFM achieves strong performance while maintaining interpretability, making it suitable for high-stakes applications.

zh.title: 可解释的基础模型，提升医疗影像分析
zh.desc: 基础模型用于从大量未标记数据中提取可转移的表示，通常通过自监督学习（SSL）实现。然而，许多模型的架构缺乏可解释性，这在医疗影像等高风险领域是一个关键问题。我们提出了DualIFM，这是一种通过BagNet骨干网设计的可解释基础模型，其小感受野生成与模型决策过程一致的类别证据图。此外，DualIFM在预训练期间加入了2D投影层，能够直接可视化表示空间，提供数据集级别的学习结构视图，包括有意义的临床聚类和潜在的虚假相关性。
